messages:
maya: Quick question on the cutover checklist — for active/active we talked about an "escrow" step so that writes from a demoted region are captured while we drain. Do we have a concise handshake definition we can put in the operator runbook?

raj: Yeah, good call. The escrow should be a *bounded* buffer with a clear TTL and owner scope. My mental model: region A sets an "escrow-mode" flag for the tenant, proxy routes writes into escrow queue, operator swaps lease, and a reconciler drains escrow into new primary once handoff acked.

sophia: Important to call out KMS/HSM implications — escrow payloads may contain PII for some tenants. We need envelope encryption keys that the receiving region can unwrap, or else escrow is useless. Also audit logs.

maya: +1 on encryption. For compliance we also need an observable assertion: "escrow queued count == drained count" with per-tenant delta tolerance. What signals should the reconciler emit?

tony: Minimal signals: escrow.enqueue, escrow.dequeue, escrow.deadletter, escrow.reconcile.success, escrow.reconcile.failure. Include counters and a histogram of time-in-escrow. Add per-tenant tags and region tag.

ops-bot: <runbook link> https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/multi-region-escrow (staging) :information_source:

elaine: I prototyped a lightweight probe that exercises the path: set tenant into escrow-mode, write a marker, swap lease, and verify marker landed. CLI snippet:```\n# set escrow-mode
curl -X POST $CONTROLPLANE/tenants/123/escrow -d '{"mode":"on","ttl":600}'
# write marker to proxy
curl -H "X-Tenant: 123" -d '{"marker":"escrow-check-$(date +%s)"}' $PROXY/v1/write
# trigger lease swap (operator)
# after swap, check reconciler
curl $OBS/escrow/tenants/123/markers | jq .
```

raj: Nice. Two more things: 1) define an expiry policy for unclaimed escrow (auto-deadletter after TTL + grace), 2) ensure cross-region time skew tolerant IDs (use monotonic vector or ULID + region prefix).

sophia: On the KMS front: recommend a cross-region key wrapping workflow — each region has a KEK in its HSM, but we derive escrow keys using a customer-specific salt so the receiving region can request unwrap only if tenant consent / policy allows. Document the policy decisions in the runbook.

maya: Agree. Also we should include an emergency fast-fail: if reconciler fails repeatedly > N attempts, fall back to synchronous forwarding to a fallback hosted model (with explicit SLA degradation) rather than risk data loss. That needs a clear operator opt-in flag.

tony: Good safety net. For metrics/alerts: set an SLO for escrow drain latency (p50/p95) and an alert if deadletter rate > 0.1% over 5m for top-100 tenants.

elaine: Will update the probe to emit the histogram and attach logs to the runbook. Passing probe will also create a short-term ticket in the cutover checklist so operator can sign-off :white_check_mark:.

maya: Action items from this thread:
- elaine: add probe and paste snippet into runbook (ETA EOD tomorrow)
- raj: write escrow state machine summary + TTL defaults (ETA 48h)
- sophia: draft KMS unwrap policy and examples (ETA 72h)
- tony: propose metric names/thresholds and a pager matrix (ETA 48h)
- ops: link the runbook into the cutover checklist and add canary gating step

ops-bot: Noted. Added task placeholders to the runbook checklist.

maya: Thanks — tagging @tony @elaine @raj @sophia for follow-up. If anyone thinks we should require a manual canary (vs automated), call it out now. I lean automated with an explicit operator approval gate for high-PII tenants. :eyes:
